title: The Trail of Patagonia's dry side
premise: Ansel Coldharbour, estranged daughter of a disgraced archaeologist, is working the dry eastern steppe of Patagonia when a dying prospector trades her a hand-drawn map for a promise to deliver it to his son. The map points to a site her father vanished chasing twenty years ago, and following it means confronting both the desert's indifference and the truth about why he left. With monsoon floods rising and a leaking boat, she and Tomás, the prospector's wary son, race upstream through canyons that swallow everything they love. At the site she finds her father's final field notes — proof he chose loyalty to a dead friend over clearing his own name — and Ansel must decide whether to publish the truth that will ruin him posthumously or honor the promise that started it all. She publishes it, and in doing so finally forgives him.
about_author: Wendell Yarrow spent a decade guiding overland expeditions across Patagonia before turning to fiction, and his prose carries the dust of those roads. He writes from a farmhouse in Chubut Province, where he keeps his late father's survey maps pinned above the desk.

chapters.title: Salt and Silence
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Working a salvage dig on the arid steppe, Ansel buries herself in routine to avoid thoughts of her estranged father. A gaunt prospector stumbles into camp, shot and feverish, clutching an oilcloth-wrapped map. Emotional beat: guarded loneliness cracked open by a stranger's desperation.

chapters.title: A Promise for a Map
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The dying man, Esteban Ruiz, trades the map for her sworn word to carry it to his son in Puerto Deseado. She recognizes the terrain sketched on it: the canyon where her father disappeared. Emotional beat: duty accepted against every instinct for self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Leaking Boat
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. She reaches Puerto Deseado and finds Tomás Ruiz, who refuses to believe his father is dead until she shows him the map — and the bullet she dug from Esteban's side. Rival treasure hunters are asking the same questions. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance forged in grief.

chapters.title: Monsoon Season
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. The rains come early and violent; the river swells past its banks as they launch upriver in Tomás's patched hull, which leaks from the first hour. They learn their pursuers, led by a man called Ferrer, bought information from someone inside town. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Canyon Keeps
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. In a sheltered overhang they find a decades-old camp: her father's initials carved beside Esteban's, proof the two men were partners once. Ansel realizes her father didn't abandon her — he was protecting Esteban's secret. Emotional beat: memory turned inside out.

chapters.title: The Crossing
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. The boat tears open on submerged rock; they lose half their supplies and nearly each other in the flood. Hauling the wreck ashore, they find evidence Ferrer's party is a day behind and closing. Emotional beat: trust cemented by shared near-death.

chapters.title: Ferrer
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ferrer catches them at a narrows and offers a bargain: the map for their lives. He reveals he was the fourth partner, the one who took the bullet meant for Esteban's silence. Ansel stalls him with a lie about a second copy. Emotional beat: love of truth tested against the price of telling it.

chapters.title: The Dry Side
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. They escape through a slot canyon only the map reveals, climbing toward the plateau where the site lies buried beneath windblown silt. Behind them, the flood has cut off retreat entirely. Emotional beat: exhaustion transfigured into awe as the land opens.

chapters.title: Field Notes
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. They uncover the site and her father's final journal: he stayed to document it rather than flee, choosing loyalty to Esteban's memory over restoring his own ruined name. Ferrer arrives, but the rising waters trap his men, and Tomás saves him anyway. Emotional beat: grief resolved into understanding.

chapters.title: What Forgives Nothing
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Downriver at last, Ansel delivers the map to no one — Tomás already carries his father home — and instead donates the site and the journal to the museum that once blacklisted her father. Publishing the truth costs her the career she built hiding from him. Emotional beat: forgiveness as the hardest dig of all.
